Blog Why Can CYBERLEEK’s Market Cap Exceed the Amount You Could Sell? Why Can CYBERLEEK’s Market Cap Exceed the Amount You Could Sell? Market Insights Jessica Updated on 2026-11-24 07:20:39 10-15m Quick Answer: Market capitalization multiplies a marginal reference price by an estimated circulating supply ; it is not a standing bid for every token. In the CoinMarketCap screenshot supplied on 24 November 2026, CYBERLEEK shows about $958,450 in market cap, 729.98 million units circulating, $1.77 million in 24-hour volume, and a 33.71% liquidity-to-market-cap indicator . None of those figures guarantees the proceeds from a large sale. A single Raydium pool observed separately on 24 November showed about $319,000 of two-sided liquidity , of which roughly half was the SOL side. A sale into that pool alone would change its price as it consumes SOL. Actual proceeds require a fresh, size-specific executable quote across available routes.
As of 24 November 2026 UTC. The screenshot is a page snapshot without a visible capture clock. DEX pool figures below are a separate observation, not a simultaneous market-wide audit. Prices and reserves can change before publication or execution.
It is a valuation convention: reference price × estimated circulating units . Using the screenshot’s rounded price of $0.001312 and circulating supply of 729.98 million gives roughly $957,000; the page’s more precise internal price yields its displayed $958,450 figure. The small rounding difference is expected. The formula values every counted unit at a price derived from marginal trades, although all units could not normally be sold at one unchanged marginal price.
The screenshot also shows 729.98 million as total and maximum supply and labels circulation at 100%. That is a statement about how the data provider classifies units, not a claim that every holder is selling or that every unit has an available buyer. The earlier Phemex investigation identified the Solana mint as ApZuxdpzMrbEYTGEzeY9afh5pj9d6qPRJCTgQYiipbKg and measured roughly 729.96 million units in an August chain snapshot. The present screenshot is consistent in scale, but a 24 November chain read would be needed to certify the exact current supply and any burns.
The screenshot’s “ FDV ” equals its market cap because the provider lists the same rounded total and circulating supply. FDV therefore adds little information under that particular data classification. It does not make all future sales possible at the displayed price. Nor does it prove that supply cannot change through every conceivable token-related event; token authority settings and chain transactions require a separate check.
Trading volume is the sum of trades over time . The same units can change hands repeatedly, and buys can offset sells. A $1.77 million 24-hour volume does not mean $1.77 million of bids waits in the book now. Even a day with many trades can have a thin order book at any one second. CMC’s “Vol/Mkt Cap” of 185.21% in the screenshot is a ratio between a rolling activity measure and a point-in-time valuation. It is not the fraction of supply a trader can sell at the last price.
The displayed liquidity-to-market-cap number is also a provider-defined indicator . The screenshot shows 33.71%, but the image does not disclose its exact pool set, reserve methodology, observation time, or whether it accounts for route depth and fees. It should not be read as a promise that 33.71% of market capitalization can be withdrawn in cash. A pool’s two-sided liquidity commonly counts both token and quote-asset sides at reference prices. A seller receives quote assets, not the combined dollar label of both sides.
The useful question is operational: How much quote asset would a sale of this size receive through a specific route at a specific time? That answer depends on pool reserves or order-book bids, fees, other orders, routing, and whether liquidity changes before the transaction lands. A tracker’s capitalization and volume columns cannot answer it alone.
The DEX Screener page for the canonical mint displayed a CYBERLEEK/SOL Raydium CPMM pool with approximately 120.87 million CYBERLEEK and 2,245.61 SOL in reserves. It labeled the token side near $159,000 and the SOL side near $159,000, producing about $319,000 combined pool liquidity . It also showed the exact pool link, beginning G8kgi and ending iMGh . These are observation-time platform figures, not a guarantee about reserves at a future block.

articles.t: GTA 6 leaker says the missing Xbox file is now out
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek says it has released the missing executable for an alleged GTA 6 leak of 209GB. Rockstar hasn't commented, and the files are unverified.
articles.txt:
The group behind the alleged GTA 6 Xbox build claims it could run on PC through emulation within a week, but the files haven’t been independently verified.
0:00 A self-described hacker group says it released the main executable for an alleged GTA 6 Xbox build, but the files haven’t been independently verified.
GTA 6 launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on 19 November, and Rockstar hasn’t announced a PC version. The group, Cyberleek, claims the community could get the game running on PC through emulation within a week at more than 30fps. No independently verified PC build has demonstrated that.
VideoCardz reported on launch day that Cyberleek had distributed roughly 209GB of files via BitTorrent. The group had already circulated pre-launch gameplay footage and promised a playable build if its meme coin reached a $30 million market cap. The coin never reached that target, and the promised build didn’t arrive.
Cyberleek described the files as a near-complete Xbox build from November 2026, but initially held back the main executable. The group said it would release that file when a countdown expired on 23 November, or sooner if its CYBERLEEK token reached a $15 million market cap. On Monday, 23 November, Cyberleek said it had released the executable, about three hours before the countdown was due to end.
In coverage of the alleged build , Cyberleek described the release as “an early Christmas gift”. The group denied accusations of a pump-and-dump scheme and used a note accompanying the executable to criticise digital-only releases, extra charges for content, and the sale of licences as purchases.
Found us on Google? Add tbreak as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Top Stories.
Xbox Series X|S consoles and modern Windows PCs share the same processor architecture, but Windows can’t simply open an Xbox game. An unofficial port would still need to account for console-specific system functions and graphics.
The cybersecurity account VX Underground says it found GTA 6 assets in the files and believes the build is genuine. Notebookcheck reports that independent projects Leonida, Xbox2Windows, and AnyXboxX are investigating whether the files could support an unofficial PC version.
An X user named Chasm posted footage that appeared to show a Windows desktop opening the game’s settings menu, with audio but no in-game graphics. The clip hasn’t been independently verified and doesn’t demonstrate playable performance.
Neither Rockstar Games nor its parent, Take-Two Interactive, has publicly commented on the latest claim. Take-Two previously described its investigation into the leaker as “rapidly evolving” and filed subpoenas seeking information from Discord about specific servers and users.
Netcraft has identified fake Cyberleek sites distributing malware or asking for cryptocurrency payments, so downloads carry risk.
